behaviors.nativeValuePresentation: Explicit iPhone sheet, including landscape regular horizontal size class; iPad anchored popover with compact system adaptation to a large sheet. Wide/short content reflow is available in a genuinely wide sheet.
behaviors.nativeValueDraft: Picker selection changes local draft only. Changed draft disables interactive dismissal; Cancel preserves entering value; Apply commits; focus returns to the original value button.
behaviors.nativeValueCandidates: Sorted, deduplicated legal grid and endpoints plus valid current/default extras. One complete-value UIPickerView column.
behaviors.editorDraft: Geometry/lens draft preview stays staged. Fixed Apply/Cancel commit/discard and return to Exposure. Dirty navigation asks Apply/Discard/Continue. Lens editing is RAW-only; raster UI evidence does not demonstrate a RAW lens draft.
behaviors.exportGuard: isEditorDraftActive covers unchanged and changed geometry/lens drafts. Export actions also guard previewRendering, previewResizePending, editor busy state and look availability.
behaviors.sourceSupport: Single JPEG/rendered DNG export supports RAW and raster; batch export remains RAW-only.
behaviors.hapticEventPolicy: Shared >=125ms gate; default > endpoint > major tick; one accepted feedback per change, no queue; app feedback suppressed for VoiceOver and omitted for native picker selection.
behaviors.hapticVerification: Source policy is recorded. Physical hardware feedback and comfort are unverified.

narrative.overview:
The native iOS and iPadOS editor uses the same restrained gray-and-yellow identity for an Operate surface: import a photo, inspect a real preview, adjust it and export. The photograph leads; system navigation, sheets, menus, SF Symbols and semantic text styles carry the interface.

This extension is scoped to `RawLab/RawLab/UI/ContentView.swift`, its Adjustments, EditorState and Panels, and `EditorComponents.swift`. The desktop prose above and in every section below remains the macOS authority. All frontmatter tokens have an `ios-` prefix and describe native points at their base size. Semantic UIKit colors and Dynamic Type styles are recorded as native source identities in the prose and sidecar; they are not converted into fixed hex values, CSS font families or invented tonal ramps. The sidecar records native components without presenting HTML/CSS approximations as SwiftUI or UIKit controls.
keyCharacteristics: A dark photo workspace with yellow functional selection.
Continuous control surfaces, a scrollable tool strip and complete numeric readouts.
Window-dependent iPhone/iPad composition and a stacked accessibility layout.
A moving horizontal ruler, a single-column system value wheel and explicit local drafts.

rules.name: The iOS State Color Rule
rules.body: Preserve semantic text colors and express selection with a visible shape or label as well as tint.

rules.name: The iOS Photo Budget Rule
rules.body: Reflow and scroll controls as the window and reading size change; keep the photograph available for evaluating the adjustment.

dos: **Do** preserve the shared processing contract, semantic system colors, system text styles and native navigation/task presentations.
**Do** keep complete values and units visible, provide 44-point action targets and retain named defaults, ranges and explicit draft actions.
**Do** preserve the fixed indicator, moving tape, local residual decay and static Reduce Motion state.
**Do** reflow by the available window and Dynamic Type; keep the selected tool and wheel draft stable across layout changes.
donts: **Don't** invent aggregate values for multi-parameter tools, shrink text into a badge, split numeric signs/decimals into separate wheels or introduce a custom numeric keyboard.
**Don't** export an active geometry/lens draft or label an unfinished preview as current.
**Don't** turn the custom ruler's lack of inertia into a change to the native picker's system behavior.
**Don't** describe authored timing as an Apple measurement, or claim Simulator images prove physical haptics, performance improvement or RAW output correctness.
